questions.q: Can TRUNCATE TABLE include a WHERE clause to remove only some rows?
options: No -- TRUNCATE TABLE is strictly all-or-nothing on the whole table
Yes, exactly like DELETE FROM
Only if the table has an IDENTITY column
Only when combined with a JOIN
questions.explain: TRUNCATE TABLE has no WHERE clause option at all -- DELETE FROM ... WHERE is the only way to remove a subset of rows.

questions.q: After DELETE FROM dbo.LessonDemo; removes all rows and a new row is inserted, what happens to the IDENTITY value?
options: It continues from where it left off -- DELETE does not reset the IDENTITY counter
It restarts at 1
It becomes NULL
SQL Server raises an error until the seed is manually reset
questions.explain: DELETE removes the rows but leaves the identity counter exactly where it was, so new rows keep numbering upward from there.

questions.q: After TRUNCATE TABLE dbo.LessonDemo; and a new row is inserted, what happens to the IDENTITY value?
options: It restarts at the seed value, e.g. 1
It continues from where it left off, same as DELETE
It skips ahead by 1000
IDENTITY columns are dropped by TRUNCATE TABLE
questions.explain: TRUNCATE TABLE resets the identity counter back to its seed value, so the next inserted row starts numbering over.

questions.q: Why does this chapter have you practice INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE against dbo.LessonDemo instead of Production.Product?
options: To avoid damaging real shared AdventureWorks2012 sample data that other students and lessons depend on
Because Production.Product does not allow any writes at all
Because dbo.LessonDemo runs faster than any real table
Because TRUNCATE TABLE only works on tables named LessonDemo
questions.explain: A mistaken DELETE or TRUNCATE against a real shared table would wipe out data others rely on -- a self-created scratch table is safe to break and re-create.

questions.q: When should you choose DELETE FROM ... WHERE over TRUNCATE TABLE?
options: When you need to remove only a subset of rows, or need the IDENTITY sequence to keep climbing
Whenever you want the fastest possible way to empty an entire table
Whenever the table has no IDENTITY column
DELETE should always be preferred over TRUNCATE TABLE in every case
questions.explain: DELETE's WHERE clause and its non-resetting IDENTITY behavior make it the right tool when you need selective removal or a continuously climbing identity sequence.
